desc:
An introduction by David and Ben Crystal to the 'Original Pronunciation' production of Shakespeare and what they reveal about the history of the English language.  

Transcript link - http://www.open.edu/openlearn/history-the-arts/culture/english-language/speaking-shakespeare-how-was-shakespeare-pronounced-when-he-was-writing 

Study a free course on Reading Shakespeare's As You Like It at the Ope

recs.stt: When Did Americans Lose Their British Accents?
recs.x:
Slightly related to this.. much study has been done into the pronunciation at the time when Shakespeare's plays were originally performed (in the 1600s) principally so that the effect can be recreated.

You can check out what it sounded like at [link] and various other videos. (Jump to 2m50s for the actual speech.)

Funnily enough, some would argue that Shakespeare in modern English also isn't real Shakespeare!

Check out the original prenounciation: [link]

I like the example of the double meaning in 'as you like it', shown at 8:11 [2].
